investors.name: WEIN Capital
investors.thesis: Accelerate Indian new-age consumer brands — helping micro-businesses and product/brand owners grow reach across online and offline retail via an omni-channel approach, plus fundraising support; enters at the product-market-fit stage.
investors.notes: India. Nascent investor/accelerator for new-age consumer/D2C brands (also weinpe.com). Founding partners are first-generation consumer-goods operators with D2C toy & gifting backgrounds; one co-founded Rowboat, a founders-and-investors community (2022). Limited public disclosure on fund size, cheque size and portfolio.
investors.writeup: WEIN Capital is an early-stage, India-focused investor and accelerator concentrating on new-age consumer brands. Its stated mission is to help micro-businesses, product makers and D2C brand owners 'go from zero to one' — entering at the product-market-fit stage and accelerating growth by expanding a brand's reach across both online channels and physical retail through an omni-channel distribution approach, while also supporting founders in raising capital. The firm is run by first-generation founders and operators with hands-on experience in the consumer-goods sector, including a D2C toy-and-gifting business; one founding partner also established Rowboat, a community launched in 2022 that connects founders and investors. WEIN positions itself around speed, low cost and growth for the brands it backs, and frames the next decade as 'India's decade' for consumer entrepreneurship. Public disclosure on the firm is currently limited — fund size, typical cheque size and a named portfolio are not publicly available — so this profile is intentionally conservative and will be expanded as verified details emerge. (Note: distinct from WEH Ventures, a separate Mumbai seed fund listed elsewhere in this sheet.)

investors.name: YourNest Venture Capital
investors.companyTypeRaw: VC (early-stage / Pre-Series A, DeepTech & B2B; SEBI AIF)
investors.thesis: Nurture global market leaders from India by backing product-led, IP-backed DeepTech and enterprise (B2B) founders; a horizontal partnership model with a high partner-to-founder ratio, concentrating efforts on a handful of companies for long-term success.
investors.notes: Gurugram. Founded 2011 by Sunil K Goyal (MD & Fund Manager; partners incl. Girish Shivani, Sanjay Pande). Three funds: Fund I (2012, $14M/INR 90 Cr, 16 cos; exits Uniphore, SmartQ; returned ~70% of corpus); Fund II (2017, $30M/INR 215 Cr, 19 DeepTech cos — Miko, Dozee, Exponent Energy); Fund III ($69M, anchored by sovereign fund NIIF). Cumulative AUM ~$53M valued ~$1.2bn (May 2025). 58 cos, 1 unicorn (Uniphore), 9 acquisitions.
investors.writeup: YourNest Venture Capital is a Gurugram-based, early-stage fund established in 2011 to nurture global market leaders from India, led by Managing Director and Fund Manager Sunil K Goyal. Sharply focused on the 'Pre-Series A' stage, it backs product-led, IP-backed startups in DeepTech — spanning AI, IoT, robotics, space tech, quantum computing, AR/VR/MR, edge cloud and health tech — alongside enterprise (B2B) software. The firm has built a thesis around India's shift from an IT-services outsourcing hub to an IP- and patent-driven 'Product Nation', and operates a distinctive horizontal partnership model with a high partner-to-founder ratio, deliberately investing in a small number of founders and concentrating its efforts on each. YourNest has launched three funds roughly every five years: Fund I (2012, ~$14M, 16 companies, with exits including Uniphore and SmartQ returning much of the corpus); Fund II (2017, ~$30M/₹215 crore, 19 deep-tech startups such as Miko, Dozee and Exponent Energy); and Fund III, a ~$69M vehicle anchored by India's sovereign National Investment and Infrastructure Fund (NIIF). Its three funds carry a cumulative AUM of about $53 million valued near $1.2 billion as of May 2025, across 58 companies that include one unicorn — conversational-AI leader Uniphore — and nine acquisitions, with the firm targeting ₹2,000 crore in AUM over the next three years.

investors.name: Pratithi Investments
investors.companyTypeRaw: Single Family Office (Kris Gopalakrishnan family) — SEBI Cat-II AIF + FoF
investors.thesis: Support entrepreneurship, technological advances and scientific research in India; back growth/late-stage startups with great founders, strong products and high standards of corporate governance, co-investing alongside leading institutional investors with a similar long-term approach.
investors.chequeSize: Late-stage debt & equity (family-office cheques); also LP commitments to funds
investors.notes: Bengaluru. Founded 2014/2015. Single family office / private investment arm of Kris Gopalakrishnan (Infosys co-founder; Padma Bhushan; chairman of Axilor Ventures). Managed via Prayog Advisors LLP; runs the Pratithi Investment Fund (SEBI Cat-II AIF). 100+ startups (81 India, 6 US), 7 unicorns (Yubi, Uniphore, XpressBees). Recent deals: Planys Technologies, Agnikul, JetSynthesys. Related family entities: Pratiksha Trust (R&D/innovation philanthropy with IISc, IIT Madras), SGK Trust (real estate).
investors.writeup: Pratithi Investments is the single family office and private investment arm of the Kris Gopalakrishnan family, founded around 2014-15 and based in Bengaluru. Kris Gopalakrishnan is a co-founder of Infosys, a Padma Bhushan awardee and chairman of the Axilor Ventures accelerator, and Pratithi reflects his conviction that the nation's growth will be fuelled by the innovation and enterprise of its people. Administered through Prayog Advisors LLP and investing via the SEBI Category-II Pratithi Investment Fund, the firm's mission is to support entrepreneurship, technological advances and scientific research in India. It is sector-agnostic and primarily backs growth and late-stage startups — across both debt and equity — while also committing as a limited partner to venture capital, private equity and debt funds across stages. Its investment approach centres on the quality of the founding team, the scale of the opportunity and a high standard of corporate governance, and it typically co-invests alongside leading institutional investors. Since launching, Pratithi has backed over a hundred startups across sectors, including seven unicorns such as Yubi, Uniphore and XpressBees, with recent participation in deep-tech and space names like Planys Technologies and Agnikul. The broader family platform also encompasses the Pratiksha Trust, which funds R&D and innovation in brain science and computing at institutions such as IISc and IIT Madras.

investors.name: Unilazer Ventures
investors.thesis: Back growth-oriented entrepreneurs building differentiated businesses
investors.notes: Ronnie Screwvala's investment fund; backed Upgrad, Ustraa
investors.writeup: Unilazer Ventures is the investment vehicle of Ronnie Screwvala, one of India's most respected entrepreneurs and the founder of UTV Group. The firm invests at Seed and Series A stages, with cheque sizes typically ranging from $500k to $5M, focusing on Consumer, D2C, FinTech, and HealthTech. What sets Unilazer apart is the value Ronnie personally brings beyond capital — deep brand-building instincts, a vast network across media, entertainment, and corporate India, and a genuine empathy for the founder journey having built and scaled businesses himself. Portfolio companies like upGrad and Ustraa reflect the firm's appetite for category-defining consumer businesses with strong brand DNA. Founders pitching to Unilazer should expect an engaged, hands-on relationship rather than a passive investor dynamic. The firm favors entrepreneurs who are building differentiated businesses with a clear path to scale, and who are not just chasing trends but are genuinely solving meaningful consumer needs. If you are an early-stage founder in a consumer-facing or digitally-enabled sector looking for a strategic partner with real operational credibility, Unilazer Ventures is worth a direct, well-prepared approach.

investors.name: Fluid Ventures
investors.thesis: Flexible and founder-friendly early-stage investing
investors.notes: India early-stage micro VC
investors.writeup: Fluid Ventures is an India-based micro VC firm focused on backing founders at the earliest stages of company building, typically at Pre-Seed and Seed. The firm writes cheques in the range of $100k to $500k, making it particularly relevant for founders raising their first institutional round or bridging into a larger Seed. Fluid Ventures invests across SaaS, FinTech, Consumer, and B2B sectors, giving it broad exposure to the Indian startup ecosystem rather than a narrow vertical focus. What distinguishes Fluid Ventures is its stated commitment to being flexible and founder-friendly, which in practice typically means faster decision-making, less bureaucratic term sheet processes, and a willingness to work around founder-specific constraints. For early-stage Indian founders who need a nimble institutional partner rather than a large fund with lengthy diligence cycles, Fluid Ventures fits well. Founders approaching the firm should be prepared to articulate early traction, product direction, and a clear sense of the Indian or global market opportunity. Given the micro VC positioning, Fluid Ventures is likely comfortable with pre-revenue or very early revenue stages, making it a practical first call for founders just beginning to build out their cap table.

investors.name: Bulleon Ventures
investors.thesis: Back ambitious founders building high-growth technology companies
investors.notes: India early-stage VC
investors.writeup: Bulleon Ventures is an India-focused early-stage venture capital firm that partners with founders at the very beginning of their journeys, typically at pre-seed and seed stages. The firm writes cheques in the range of $100,000 to $500,000, making it relevant for founders raising their first institutional capital or building conviction ahead of a larger seed round. Bulleon's sectoral focus spans SaaS, FinTech, Consumer, and B2B businesses, reflecting an interest in technology-driven models with strong unit economics potential and scalable distribution. The firm's stated orientation toward ambitious founders signals an appetite for bold market theses rather than incremental ideas. For Indian founders, Bulleon represents a domestically rooted investor that understands the nuances of building in India, including market timing, distribution challenges, and the path from early traction to Series A readiness. Founders approaching Bulleon should come prepared with a clear articulation of the problem, early evidence of product-market fit or strong founder-market fit, and a compelling view of how the business scales. Given the cheque size, Bulleon is often a lead or co-lead investor at pre-seed and can be a meaningful anchor for seed rounds.

investors.name: Ideaspring Capital
investors.thesis: Back product-led startups with deep IP and global potential
investors.notes: Bangalore-based product-led B2B VC; backed CloudSEK, Juspay
investors.writeup: Ideaspring Capital is a Bangalore-based venture capital firm purpose-built for Indian product startups targeting global markets. The firm invests at Seed and Pre-Series A stages, writing cheques in the range of $250,000 to $2 million, making it well-suited for founders who have early product-market signal and are ready to scale their go-to-market or deepen their technology stack. Ideaspring's thesis is firmly centered on product-led companies in SaaS, DeepTech, AI, IoT, and Enterprise software, with a clear preference for businesses where proprietary IP creates lasting competitive advantage. The team brings operational and entrepreneurial depth, which founders often cite as a differentiator beyond just capital. Portfolio companies like CloudSEK and Juspay reflect the firm's appetite for technically ambitious, category-defining bets with genuine international reach. Founders building in B2B spaces where the product itself drives distribution and retention will find Ideaspring's philosophy closely aligned. If you are a founding team with a strong engineering core, early enterprise traction, and a credible path to global customers, Ideaspring Capital is worth a direct conversation at the earliest stages of your fundraise.

investors.name: Fireside Ventures
investors.thesis: Partner with founder-led consumer brands building India's next iconic companies
investors.notes: India's leading D2C/consumer brand fund; backed Mamaearth, Boat, MCaffeine
investors.writeup: Fireside Ventures is one of India's most prominent early-stage funds dedicated exclusively to consumer brands. The fund focuses on founder-led businesses operating in D2C, FMCG, personal care, food and beverage, and consumer health, with a clear thesis around backing brands that can build deep consumer affinity and scale through both online and offline channels. Fireside is particularly well-suited for founders who have demonstrated early product-market fit and are looking for a partner who understands the nuances of building a consumer brand in India, from storytelling and community to supply chain and retail distribution. The team brings hands-on operational experience and a strong network across retail, marketing, and manufacturing ecosystems. Portfolio companies have benefited from Fireside's active involvement in brand positioning, hiring, and go-to-market strategy beyond just capital. If you are building a consumer brand targeting the aspirational Indian consumer, Fireside should be a priority conversation. They typically engage at Seed through Series A stages with cheque sizes ranging from approximately $500k to $5 million, and prefer founders who combine authentic brand vision with execution clarity.

investors.name: Rukam Capital
investors.thesis: Invest in mission-driven founders building scalable businesses
investors.notes: India early-stage VC; women-led fund
investors.writeup: Rukam Capital is an early-stage venture capital firm investing in India's most promising Seed and Pre-Series A startups. As a women-led fund, Rukam brings a differentiated perspective to founder evaluation, placing strong emphasis on mission-driven founders who are building businesses with genuine consumer or market impact. The firm writes cheques in the range of $250,000 to $2 million, making it well-suited for founders raising their first institutional round or bridging toward a Series A. Rukam's sector focus spans consumer brands, direct-to-consumer businesses, HealthTech, FinTech, and SaaS, reflecting a belief that both digitally-native consumer models and B2B tech platforms can generate durable, scalable returns in the Indian market. Founders can expect a hands-on, collaborative working relationship with the Rukam team, which brings operational and strategic support beyond just capital. For founders who are early in their fundraising journey and building businesses that solve real problems for Indian consumers or enterprises, Rukam Capital represents a meaningful early institutional partner to have in your corner.

investors.name: TPG NewQuest
investors.thesis: Partner with entrepreneurs in Asia to grow industry-leading businesses
investors.notes: Asia-focused PE; invested in Vedantu, Star Health, Vistaar
investors.writeup: TPG NewQuest is the Asia-focused private equity platform operating under the broader TPG umbrella, one of the world's leading alternative asset management firms. In India, the firm targets growth-stage and mature businesses across consumer, fintech, healthcare, B2B services, and manufacturing — sectors where scale and operational improvement can drive meaningful value creation. Their typical engagement is with companies that have moved well past early traction and are looking for a credible institutional partner to fund significant expansion, market consolidation, or liquidity events. Cheque sizes in the $20M to $150M range mean they are relevant for Series B and beyond, as well as structured growth rounds. Founders should note that TPG NewQuest brings not just capital but access to the broader TPG global network, which can be advantageous for companies with cross-border ambitions or those seeking strategic introductions in other Asian markets. Their portfolio construction reflects a preference for businesses with defensible market positions and capable management teams. For Indian founders raising a significant growth round, TPG NewQuest is worth engaging early given their longer diligence cycles typical of institutional PE investors.

investors.name: 12 Flags
investors.thesis: Invest in founders from emerging countries building global businesses
investors.notes: Cross-border early-stage VC
investors.writeup: 12 Flags is a cross-border early-stage venture capital firm that backs founders from emerging markets building businesses with global ambition. For Indian founders, this is a meaningful distinction: 12 Flags is not primarily a domestic-India fund but a firm that specifically seeks out founders from markets like India who are solving problems at a global scale. Their focus sectors span SaaS, FinTech, Consumer, AI, and B2B, giving them broad coverage across the most active segments of the Indian startup ecosystem. Cheque sizes range from $100k to $500k, making them relevant at the pre-seed and seed stages when founders are still validating product-market fit or preparing for their first institutional round. Founders who are building products designed to compete internationally—rather than those purely optimising for domestic distribution—will resonate most strongly with the 12 Flags thesis. The firm's cross-border perspective also means they may bring value beyond capital, including access to networks across multiple emerging markets, which can be useful for founders eyeing expansion into Southeast Asia, the Middle East, or other high-growth geographies alongside their India base.

investors.name: The Fundamentum Partnership
investors.thesis: Partner with growth-stage tech companies building for India and global markets
investors.notes: Founded by Nandan Nilekani and Sanjeev Aggarwal; backed Kissht, Khatabook
investors.writeup: Fundamentum Partnership is a growth-stage venture fund founded by two of India's most respected technology and investing figures: Nandan Nilekani and Sanjeev Aggarwal. The firm targets companies at Series A and Series B that have moved past early validation and are building toward significant scale. Their focus spans SaaS, consumer tech, fintech, B2B platforms, and increasingly AI-enabled businesses. What sets Fundamentum apart for founders is the depth of its operating experience. Nandan Nilekani's involvement gives portfolio companies rare access to policy circles, large enterprise relationships, and credibility that is difficult to replicate. Sanjeev Aggarwal brings decades of hands-on venture investing and company building experience across Indian tech ecosystems. Cheque sizes typically range from five to twenty-five million dollars, making Fundamentum most relevant for startups that have clear revenue traction and a defined path to operational scale. The fund takes an active, partnership-oriented approach rather than passive board participation, and founders frequently cite the quality of strategic guidance as a differentiator. If you are a growth-stage founder with strong fundamentals building a technology business for India or India-plus-global markets, Fundamentum is a serious and well-networked partner to pursue.

investors.name: Whiteboard Capital
investors.thesis: Invest in early-stage product companies solving real problems
investors.notes: India early-stage VC; backed Nua, Recykal, Juspay
investors.writeup: Whiteboard Capital is an India-focused early-stage venture fund that partners with founders building product-first companies tackling genuine, large-scale problems. The firm typically writes cheques in the $250K to $2M range at Seed and Pre-Series A, making it relevant for founders who are past the idea stage but still in the process of establishing early product-market fit. Whiteboard has built a portfolio that reflects a clear preference for businesses where product depth and technology form the core competitive moat, as evidenced by investments in companies like Juspay in payments infrastructure, Nua in consumer health, and Recykal in sustainability tech. The team is known for being founder-friendly and hands-on, particularly valuable during the early company-building phase when strategic input matters as much as capital. Their sector interest spans SaaS, FinTech, Consumer, AI, and B2B, giving them breadth across the Indian startup ecosystem. Founders approaching Whiteboard should come prepared with a sharp articulation of the problem they are solving, a clear view of their product differentiation, and early signals of traction. The fund is best suited for Indian founders building scalable, technology-led businesses from the ground up.

investors.name: Sofina
investors.thesis: Make long-term investments in growth companies across technology and consumer sectors
investors.notes: Belgian investment group; backed Byju's, Vedantu, Teachmint
investors.writeup: Sofina is a Belgian family-controlled investment group with a significant and active presence in the Indian startup ecosystem, particularly in EdTech and consumer technology. The firm operates with a long-term investment philosophy, distinguishing itself from traditional VC funds by avoiding pressure to exit within a fixed fund lifecycle. This makes Sofina an attractive partner for founders who want a stable, committed backer during the growth phase rather than one focused purely on near-term returns. Sofina typically engages at Series B and later stages, writing large cheques that can support sustained scaling, international expansion, and operational maturity. Their India portfolio reflects a strong conviction around EdTech, as seen through investments in Byju's, Vedantu, and Teachmint, but the firm also evaluates opportunities across consumer, FinTech, SaaS, and healthcare. Founders should expect a diligence process aligned with Sofina's global standards, with emphasis on unit economics, leadership quality, and long-term market opportunity. Sofina is best suited for founders who have demonstrated product-market fit and are now focused on building enduring, large-scale businesses in India.

investors.name: BAT VC
investors.thesis: Back ambitious founders building technology companies
investors.notes: India early-stage micro VC
investors.writeup: BAT VC is an India-focused micro VC operating at the earliest stages of company building, writing cheques from $50k to $500k at pre-seed and seed. The fund is built around backing ambitious founders who are developing technology-driven businesses across SaaS, FinTech, Consumer, and AI verticals. As a micro VC, BAT VC typically moves with speed and conviction compared to larger institutional funds, which can be a significant advantage for founders who need a fast, decisive first check to get going. Their sector focus reflects the core themes driving India's current startup cycle, from enterprise software and embedded finance to AI-native products and consumer internet plays. Founders raising their first or second institutional round will find BAT VC relevant as a lead or co-investor capable of writing meaningful early capital without requiring the traction thresholds that larger funds demand. Given their stage focus, they are well suited to engage with founders who are still in the zero-to-one phase, whether that means pre-revenue or early product-market fit exploration. Indian founders building scalable, technology-led businesses should consider BAT VC as a practical early partner in their fundraising conversations.

investors.name: Kriscore Capital
investors.thesis: Invest in early-stage founders disrupting large markets
investors.notes: India micro VC
investors.writeup: Kriscore Capital is an India-focused micro VC that operates at the Pre-Seed and Seed stages, writing cheques between $50,000 and $300,000. The firm is sector-focused across SaaS, FinTech, Consumer, and B2B, which covers a broad sweep of the Indian startup landscape while still maintaining thematic clarity. For founders, this means Kriscore is best approached when you are at the idea-to-early-traction stage and looking for an investor who can move quickly and with conviction without requiring the proof points that larger institutional funds typically demand. Their thesis around backing founders disrupting large markets suggests they value ambitious market sizing and founder quality above all else. As a micro VC, Kriscore likely brings a hands-on and accessible approach compared to larger funds, which can be particularly valuable for first-time founders navigating early product, go-to-market, and team-building decisions. Founders in SaaS or FinTech with a clear India-first or India-to-global narrative are likely to resonate well with their investment lens. Reaching out via LinkedIn is a practical first step given the firm's relatively lean profile.

investors.name: Synapses VC
investors.thesis: Invest in neuro-inspired and neurotechnology companies
investors.notes: Deep tech focused fund
investors.writeup: Synapses VC is a deep tech focused early-stage fund that invests at the Pre-Seed and Seed stages, writing cheques between $100,000 and $500,000. Their core thesis centers on neuro-inspired and neurotechnology companies, making them one of the few funds globally with a dedicated focus on this emerging category. Beyond pure neurotechnology, they also engage with broader DeepTech, HealthTech, and AI opportunities, particularly where there is a meaningful intersection with how intelligence, cognition, or biological systems are modeled or augmented. For Indian founders working on brain-computer interfaces, neuromorphic computing, cognitive health platforms, AI architectures inspired by neural systems, or related deep science applications, Synapses VC represents a strategically aligned early partner. Their specialist positioning means they are likely to add value beyond capital, bringing domain-specific networks and technical diligence that generalist funds cannot match. Founders approaching them should be prepared to articulate the neuro-inspired or neurotechnology angle clearly, demonstrate scientific credibility, and show a credible path from research insight to scalable product. Their cheque range is suitable for pre-product or early-traction rounds where capital efficiency and the right thematic investor matter more than sheer fund size.

investors.name: BoldCap
investors.thesis: Back bold founders taking on large challenges
investors.notes: India early-stage micro VC
investors.writeup: BoldCap is an India-focused micro VC that operates at the earliest stages of company building, typically writing cheques between $100k and $500k at pre-seed and seed. The firm is built around a straightforward conviction: back bold founders who are willing to take on large, hard challenges in markets that matter. Their sector focus spans SaaS, FinTech, Consumer, AI, and B2B, which covers much of the high-growth opportunity landscape in India today. As a micro VC, BoldCap tends to be more accessible and faster-moving than larger institutional funds, which can be a meaningful advantage for founders who need a quick, decisive first cheque. Founders approaching BoldCap should come prepared with a clear articulation of the scale of the problem they are solving and a sharp point of view on why they are the right team to go after it. The firm is unlikely to be moved by incremental or derivative ideas. If you are building something ambitious in one of their core sectors and are at the earliest stage of your journey, BoldCap is worth a direct, concise outreach. Their India grounding means they understand the local market dynamics, distribution challenges, and unit economics realities that shape early-stage building in the Indian context.

investors.name: IN44 Capital
investors.thesis: Invest in India's most ambitious early-stage founders
investors.notes: India early-stage micro VC
investors.writeup: IN44 Capital is an India-focused micro VC that backs early-stage founders at the Pre-Seed and Seed stages. The firm operates with a clear mandate: find and back India's most ambitious builders before the market catches on. With a typical cheque size of $100,000 to $500,000, IN44 is particularly relevant for founders raising their first institutional capital or a lean seed round where a value-add lead or co-investor can meaningfully move the needle. The firm concentrates on sectors where Indian startups have demonstrated strong global competitiveness, including SaaS, FinTech, Consumer, AI, and B2B. Given its micro VC positioning, founders can expect a more direct relationship with the decision-makers, faster conviction cycles, and hands-on support during the earliest and most uncertain stages of company building. IN44 Capital is well-suited for founders who are pre-product-market fit but have a sharp thesis, early traction signals, or a differentiated insight into their market. If you are building in one of their core sectors and are raising a Pre-Seed or Seed round in India, IN44 Capital is a practical first conversation to have.

investors.name: Bluehill.vc
investors.thesis: Back founders building high-growth technology companies
investors.notes: Early-stage VC
investors.writeup: Bluehill.vc is an early-stage venture capital firm that partners with founders at the pre-seed and seed stages, when the need for conviction-led capital is highest and the margin for error is lowest. The firm focuses on high-growth technology companies across SaaS, FinTech, Consumer, and AI, sectors that continue to see strong momentum in the Indian startup ecosystem. With a typical cheque size ranging from $100k to $500k, Bluehill is well-positioned to lead or participate in a founder's first meaningful institutional round, offering capital that can help validate a product, build an early team, or push toward initial revenue milestones. For Indian founders, this positioning is particularly relevant as the pre-seed and seed landscape has historically been fragmented and underserved by larger funds. Bluehill's sector focus aligns with where Indian startups are generating global-scale opportunities today. Founders approaching Bluehill should come prepared with a clear articulation of the problem they are solving, early evidence of product-market fit or a credible path to it, and a long-term vision for building a technology-led business with meaningful growth potential.

investors.name: Gaurav Sharma
investors.thesis: Gaurav Sharma backs early-stage Indian founders at Pre-Seed, focusing on D2C, Logistics, Web3, CleanTech, and DeepTech with a conviction-driven, hands-on approach.
investors.notes: Gaurav is an individual angel investor active at the Pre-Seed stage with a reported cheque size of around $1M. He covers a broad but emerging-technology-leaning mandate across D2C, Logistics, Web3, CleanTech, and DeepTech sectors.
investors.writeup: Gaurav Sharma is an individual angel investor operating at the Pre-Seed stage in the Indian startup ecosystem. His investment interest spans five distinct but forward-looking verticals: D2C, Logistics, Web3, CleanTech, and DeepTech, reflecting a preference for founders building at the intersection of technology and real-world impact. With a cheque size of approximately $1M, Gaurav is positioned to be a meaningful early backer for founders who are raising their very first institutional or semi-institutional round. At Pre-Seed, investors like Gaurav typically value strong founder-market fit, a clear problem hypothesis, and early signals of traction or domain depth rather than polished metrics. Founders approaching Gaurav should come prepared with a sharp articulation of the problem they are solving, why India is the right market, and how their chosen sector intersects with scalable technology. Given the breadth of his sectoral interest, he appears open to both consumer-facing and deep-technology bets, making him a versatile angel for founders across these categories. A warm introduction through mutual network connections in the Indian angel or startup community is likely the most effective way to get on his radar.

investors.name: Bharat Angels Fund
investors.thesis: Bharat Angels Fund backs early-stage Indian startups at Pre-Seed and Seed stages across high-growth sectors, with a focus on capital-efficient businesses solving real problems for Indian consumers and enterprises.
investors.notes: Bharat Angels Fund operates as a structured angel network and early-stage VC, typically deploying cheques in the INR 2.5L–7.5L range per deal. The fund covers a broad sector mandate including SaaS, D2C, FinTech, CleanTech, DeepTech, PropTech, and B2B Marketplaces, making it relevant for diverse early-stage founders.
investors.writeup: Bharat Angels Fund is an early-stage investment platform focused on Pre-Seed and Seed stage startups in India. The fund operates with a wide sector aperture, covering SaaS for both enterprise and SMB segments, B2B Marketplaces, D2C brands, FinTech, Consumer Internet, CleanTech, DeepTech, PropTech, and the Creator Economy. This breadth makes it a relevant conversation for founders across most high-traction verticals in the Indian startup ecosystem. Typical cheque sizes range from INR 2.5 lakh to INR 7.5 lakh, positioning the fund as a meaningful participant in early rounds alongside other angels or micro-VCs. For founders at the idea or early traction stage, Bharat Angels Fund can provide not just capital but access to a network of angels who often bring domain expertise, introductions, and follow-on support. Founders should approach with a clear articulation of the Indian market opportunity, a defensible business model, and early proof of concept or customer traction. Given the structured angel network format, expect a collaborative diligence process involving multiple members before a final investment decision is reached.

investors.name: Huddle Ventures
investors.thesis: Huddle Ventures backs early-stage Indian startups at Pre-Seed to Pre-Series A, writing small but meaningful cheques to help founders validate and scale across sectors, with a focus on founder-first support and community-driven growth.
investors.notes: Neuropixel.ai, Celcius Logistics, StepSetGo, HuddleUp.ai, Mykare Health, Vama
investors.writeup: Huddle Ventures is an early-stage venture capital firm investing at the Pre-Seed, Seed, and Pre-Series A stages across all sectors in India. With a typical cheque size of around Rs 2 lakh, Huddle is best suited for founders at the earliest stages of company building who need not just capital but community and infrastructure support. What differentiates Huddle is its integrated model: the firm operates out of a co-working and collaboration platform, meaning portfolio founders often benefit from proximity to other early-stage teams, mentors, and operators within the Huddle ecosystem. Their portfolio reflects genuine sector agnosticism, spanning AI with Neuropixel.ai, mental health with HuddleUp.ai, fitness with StepSetGo, healthcare with Mykare Health, and logistics with Celsius Logistics. For founders raising their first institutional or semi-institutional round, Huddle can be a strategic early backer who brings community alongside capital. Given the small cheque size, founders typically approach Huddle as part of a broader pre-seed round rather than a lead investor. Outreach via LinkedIn or through the Huddle co-working community tends to work well.

investors.name: Emphasis Ventures (EMVC)
investors.thesis: Invest in founders building large-scale businesses at the intersection of technology and commerce
investors.notes: Slice, Khatabook, M2P, Jar and more
investors.writeup: Emphasis Ventures (EMVC) is an early-stage venture capital firm investing in Indian founders who are building technology-driven businesses across commerce, financial services, and the digital economy. Their sweet spot spans Pre-Seed to Series A, with cheque sizes ranging from $100,000 to $1,000,000, making them well-suited for founders who are past initial validation but still building out their core teams and growth engines. EMVC has demonstrated a consistent ability to identify breakout companies early, with portfolio names like Slice, Khatabook, M2P, and Jar reflecting their conviction in FinTech infrastructure and SMB digitisation themes. Beyond FinTech, they actively look at enterprise and SMB SaaS, B2B marketplaces, logistics, consumer eCommerce, and the Creator Economy. Founders can expect EMVC to engage seriously on go-to-market strategy, unit economics, and the technology architecture underlying the business model. Their thesis is rooted in the belief that the most durable Indian companies will be built at the convergence of technology and commerce. If you are a founder targeting large addressable markets in these sectors and raising an early institutional round, EMVC is a relevant and well-networked partner to approach.

investors.name: The Venture Guys
investors.thesis: The Venture Guys is an India-based syndicate backing early-stage startups across all sectors at Pre-Seed, Seed, and Pre-Series A stages, writing cheques around $1M by pooling capital from a curated network of investors.
investors.notes: Operates as a syndicate model, meaning deal-by-deal participation rather than a traditional blind-pool fund. Founders get access to a collective of angels and operators rather than a single decision-maker. Active across sectors, making it accessible to startups outside niche verticals.
investors.writeup: The Venture Guys is an Indian investment syndicate that backs early-stage founders from Pre-Seed through Pre-Series A. Unlike traditional VC funds, the syndicate model means capital is raised deal-by-deal from a network of investors, which can result in faster initial conversations but may require the lead to rally co-investors before a cheque closes. Their standard deployment size sits around $1M per deal, positioning them well for rounds where a founder needs a meaningful anchor or co-lead alongside other investors. Because they invest across all sectors, founders from consumer tech, SaaS, fintech, deeptech, or D2C are all fair game. The practical implication for founders is that a strong relationship with the syndicate lead matters enormously since that person champions your deal internally to the broader network. Prepare a tight investment memo alongside your pitch deck, as syndicate members often review materials asynchronously. Given their India focus and early-stage mandate, traction validation, founder-market fit, and a clear path to the next institutional round are likely the key diligence levers. Ideal for founders seeking not just capital but a distributed set of operator-investors who can open doors across the Indian startup ecosystem.

investors.name: Eques Capital
investors.thesis: Eques Capital backs early-stage Indian startups from Pre-Seed through Series A across technology-driven sectors including SaaS, D2C, FinTech, and DeepTech, with a focus on founders building scalable, high-impact businesses.
investors.notes: Cusmat, Rukart, Collekto
investors.criteria: First criterion are the Product, Market, Founder fit. We then seek business model, Revenue model, market, growth & scalability, promoter integrity and vision, on-ground verification of business, potential risks and mitigation strategies, Moat and capability to disrupt the market.
investors.processNotes: We do not believe merely in board-room management rather we work shoulder to shoulder with the promoter to take the company forward. We do provide a 360 degree ecosystem to our portfolio companies and provide decisive leadership and strong expertise in business transformation which addresses the gaps in businesses, and paves way for optimal value creation by unlocking the true potential of the business.
investors.writeup: Eques Capital is an Indian venture capital firm that invests across a broad spectrum of early-stage startups, from Pre-Seed all the way through Series A. Their portfolio signals an appetite for both B2B technology plays and consumer-facing businesses, spanning enterprise SaaS, B2B marketplaces, D2C brands, FinTech, Logistics, HealthTech, CleanTech, DeepTech, PropTech, Creator Economy, and ESG-aligned ventures. The firm's cheque size flexibility, ranging from $15,000 to $2,000,000, means they can engage meaningfully with founders at very different stages of capital need, from a founder running early pilots to a startup ready for a structured Seed round. Known portfolio companies include Cusmat in enterprise learning, Rukart in B2B commerce, and Collekto in FinTech-driven debt collections, suggesting they appreciate founders solving real operational inefficiencies in underserved markets. For Indian founders, Eques Capital represents a generalist early-stage partner willing to engage across sectors and ticket sizes, making them worth approaching with a clear problem statement, early traction, and a strong view on the Indian market opportunity.

investors.name: Originity (Origin To Eternity LLP)
investors.thesis: Originity backs early-stage startups at Pre-Seed through Pre-Series A in Health Tech, CleanTech, and Education, writing focused cheques of $20,000–$50,000 to founders building purposeful, impact-oriented businesses.
investors.notes: https://angel.co/sachinoswal
investors.processNotes: I invest my time, money & energy behind startups that I love.
investors.writeup: Originity, operating under the LLP Origin To Eternity, is a family office investing at the earliest stages of a startup's journey — Pre-Seed, Seed, and Pre-Series A. With a typical cheque size ranging from $20,000 to $50,000, Originity is suited for founders who are raising their first institutional or near-institutional round and need a committed, values-aligned backer rather than a large institutional fund. The investment focus spans three sectors with significant India relevance: Health Tech, CleanTech, and Education. These are areas where technology-driven solutions can create meaningful impact at scale across Tier 1 and Tier 2 India. The family office structure means founders can expect a more direct and personal relationship with the principal, faster decision-making cycles, and a patient capital outlook compared to a traditional VC fund with LP pressure. The AngelList presence indicates openness to engaging with founders through digital platforms and syndicated rounds. Founders approaching Originity should come with a clear problem statement, early traction or validation in their target sector, and an articulate view on how their work drives long-term impact alongside commercial returns.

investors.name: 77 Capital
investors.thesis: 77 Capital backs early-stage Indian startups at Pre-Seed and Seed stages, focusing on SaaS, B2B marketplaces, FinTech, and HealthTech through a syndicate model that brings together aligned capital and operator networks.
investors.notes: Mewt, Fego, Clinikally, Vidyut Tech, M2P, Hyperface
investors.criteria: Tend to turnaround quickly, primarily calls with the founders + 3rd party due diligence (if required)
investors.processNotes: Primarily Focussed on Fintech as 77 Capital + focus on other sectors in individual capacity
investors.writeup: 77 Capital is an Indian investment syndicate that writes cheques of USD 75,000 to 100,000 into Pre-Seed and Seed stage startups. Its portfolio reflects a clear conviction around B2B software and infrastructure businesses, with investments spanning enterprise and SMB SaaS, B2B marketplaces, fintech, and health tech. Companies like M2P and Hyperface signal comfort with fintech infrastructure and API-led business models, while Clinikally and Fego point to interest in digital health and consumer wellness built on strong tech foundations. Vidyut Tech and Mewt further demonstrate a pattern of backing asset-light, scalable Indian startups solving real enterprise or platform problems. As a syndicate, 77 Capital offers founders more than just capital; the model typically means co-investors and domain-relevant angels come in alongside the lead, which can be valuable for startups seeking both money and market access. Founders pitching to 77 Capital should be prepared to articulate clear unit economics, a defensible B2B go-to-market strategy, and a path to scalable revenue. The typical entry point is early enough to help shape the company, making a crisp product narrative and a strong founding team the most important factors in the conversation.

investors.name: O2 Angel Network LLP
investors.thesis: O2 Angel Network backs early-stage Indian startups across all sectors, writing syndicated cheques from pre-seed through Series B, with a preference for technology-driven and deep-tech ventures solving real-world problems.
investors.notes: Skye, Eeki Foods, Green Tiger, BosonQ PSI, Navars, Tutti Frutti, Amaara Herbs, Fabheads, Cultyvate, ZiffyTech, Urban Matrix, Brainwired,
investors.writeup: O2 Angel Network LLP is an India-based angel syndicate that deploys capital across the full early-stage spectrum, from pre-seed ideation through Series B growth rounds. Operating as a syndicate, the network aggregates commitments from multiple angels to write meaningful cheques in the USD 100K to USD 500K range, giving founders a structured and credible investor on their cap table rather than a fragmented collection of individual angels. The portfolio reflects genuine sector diversity, spanning deep-tech and simulation software through BosonQ PSI, advanced materials manufacturing through Fabheads, food and agri-tech through Eeki Foods and Cultyvate, consumer wellness through Amaara Herbs and Tutti Frutti, healthtech through ZiffyTech, and urban mobility through Urban Matrix. This breadth signals that O2 evaluates founders and market opportunity over rigid sectoral mandates. For early-stage founders in India who need both capital and network leverage, O2 Angel Network offers the combined conviction of a coordinated angel group with the flexibility typical of early-stage syndicate investing. Founders pitching here should be prepared to articulate a clear problem statement, a defensible solution, and a scalable India or global market opportunity.

investors.name: Long Tail Ventures
investors.thesis: Long Tail Ventures backs early-stage Indian startups at Pre-Seed to Pre-Series A with small but conviction-led cheques, focusing on capital-efficient businesses across SaaS, B2B marketplaces, D2C, FinTech, and emerging sectors like Web3, CleanTech, and DeepTech.
investors.notes: Clinikally, ZFW Dark Stores, STAGE, Elixir Protocol, etc.
investors.processNotes: As operators from India & the US----- we move quick (2 calls max) & can bring in our global network of founders, funds, & CXOs.
investors.writeup: Long Tail Ventures is an early-stage venture capital firm writing cheques between USD 35,000 and USD 100,000 across Pre-Seed, Seed, and Pre-Series A rounds in India. The firm takes a broad sectoral stance, backing founders in SaaS for enterprise and SMB, B2B marketplaces, eCommerce and D2C brands, FinTech, Logistics, Health Tech, Consumer Internet, Web3, CleanTech, DeepTech, and DevTools. The portfolio reflects genuine range: Clinikally in D2C health and skincare, ZFW Dark Stores in quick commerce infrastructure, STAGE in regional language streaming, and Elixir Protocol in the Web3 space. For founders, the relatively small cheque size means Long Tail Ventures is often accessible at the very first institutional moment, making it a practical first call for pre-revenue or early-revenue teams building in India. Given the breadth of sectors covered, founders should lead with product differentiation and a clear path to scalable unit economics. The firm appears comfortable with unconventional or niche market theses, consistent with its name and the idea that meaningful outcomes can emerge from underexplored corners of the market.

investors.name: Singhvi Heritage LLP / JITO Angel Network
investors.thesis: Singhvi Heritage LLP, operating through the JITO Angel Network, backs early-stage Indian startups across sectors at the pre-seed to pre-Series A stage, with a preference for founders building scalable, technology-driven businesses with strong unit economics.
investors.notes: BluSmart, VideoVerse, ChargeGrid, Rooter
investors.writeup: Singhvi Heritage LLP participates in early-stage startup investing through the JITO Angel Network, one of India's more active community-anchored angel platforms. The JITO Angel Network draws on a wide base of high-net-worth individuals and family offices from the Jain entrepreneurial community, giving founders access not just to capital but to a dense network of business operators, traders, and industrialists with pan-India reach. The portfolio signals a clear appetite for technology-enabled businesses across diverse verticals — from electric mobility and EV charging infrastructure with BluSmart and ChargeGrid, to media-tech and sports gaming through VideoVerse and Rooter. This breadth suggests the investor is sector-agnostic at the early stage, prioritising founder quality and market potential over vertical specialisation. Cheque sizes in the $20,000 to $50,000 range make this a relevant partner for pre-seed and seed rounds, either as a lead or alongside other angels. Founders who can demonstrate a connection to the JITO community or present at JITO-affiliated pitch forums may find warm introductions easier to secure. The family office backing also suggests patient, relationship-oriented capital rather than purely return-driven institutional pressure.

investors.name: Sprout Venture Partners
investors.thesis: Sprout Venture Partners backs early-stage Indian startups at Pre-Seed and Seed stages across sectors, writing cheques of around Rs 40–42 lakh (approximately $500K) to help founders validate and scale their core business model.
investors.notes: Pixis, Ripplr, Advantage Club, Fashor, Advarisk, Rusk Media
investors.writeup: Sprout Venture Partners is an early-stage venture capital firm focused on Pre-Seed and Seed investments in Indian startups. The firm takes a sector-agnostic stance, having backed companies across AI-driven marketing technology, B2B distribution, employee engagement, fashion D2C, risk analytics, and the creator economy. This breadth signals that Sprout evaluates founders and market opportunity rather than restricting itself to a narrow vertical. With a cheque size of around $500,000, it is well suited for founders raising their first institutional round or a bridge into a larger Seed. The portfolio names suggest comfort with both technology-first and operationally intensive business models, which is a useful signal for founders across the startup spectrum. Founders approaching Sprout should be ready to articulate a clear problem statement, early traction or validation metrics, and a compelling view on why their market is large and defensible in the Indian context. Given the early stage focus, the team and founder-market fit are likely weighted heavily in evaluation. Engagement through their LinkedIn or website is a reasonable first step, and warm introductions through portfolio founders or ecosystem intermediaries will typically improve response rates.

investors.name: Sparrow Capital
investors.thesis: Sparrow Capital backs early-stage Indian startups at Pre-Seed and Seed stages across high-growth sectors including SaaS, FinTech, B2B Marketplace, and Consumer Internet, focusing on founder-first investing with conviction at the earliest stages.
investors.notes: Fund investments- Groyyo, Probo, Mailmodo, goKwik
investors.criteria: We strive towards building a unique point of view on a space or sector or a company. We partner with deep conviction. ​ We strive to practice intellectual honesty and admit when we are wrong (we often are). ​ We treat people with respect. Give entrepreneurs "an answer" in a timely manner.
investors.writeup: Sparrow Capital is an early-stage venture capital firm investing across Pre-Seed and Seed rounds in India. The firm has a broad sectoral appetite spanning SaaS for both enterprise and SMB customers, B2B Marketplaces, eCommerce, FinTech, Logistics, Health Tech, Consumer Internet, CleanTech, PropTech, DevTools, Creator Economy, and TravelTech. This breadth signals a thesis centered on backing strong founders and market timing rather than restricting to a single vertical. Their portfolio reflects a good read on emerging Indian internet themes, with bets on Groyyo in B2B supply chain, Probo in consumer fintech, Mailmodo in SaaS, and goKwik in eCommerce infrastructure. With a typical cheque size of around Rs 5 lakhs, Sparrow Capital operates at the very first institutional entry point, making them relevant for founders raising their first external capital. Founders approaching Sparrow Capital should come with a clear problem statement, early market validation, and a compelling narrative around why their sector is poised for scale in the Indian context. Their lean cheque size suggests they value conviction-based early partnership over large initial positions.

investors.name: Piper Serica Angel Fund
investors.thesis: Piper Serica Angel Fund backs early-stage Indian startups at Pre-Series A and Series A, with a broad sectoral appetite spanning SaaS, FinTech, DeepTech, CleanTech, and consumer internet, seeking founders building scalable, differentiated businesses.
investors.notes: Alt Mobility, Oditly, Crediwatch, ZFW Dark stores, Driffle
investors.criteria: We typically focus on tech startups where tech is the main USP and can be leveraged to scale exponentially
investors.processNotes: We dont invest in D2C brands.
investors.writeup: Piper Serica Angel Fund is an early-stage venture vehicle associated with the Piper Serica brand, which has built a strong reputation in Indian markets for disciplined, research-oriented investing. The fund participates at Pre-Series A and Series A stages, writing cheques in the INR 3–5 lakh range, making it relevant for founders looking for committed angel-level institutional backing alongside larger rounds. The fund maintains a deliberately wide sectoral mandate, covering SaaS for enterprise and SMB, FinTech, DeepTech, CleanTech, Web3, gaming, logistics, health tech, PropTech, creator economy, and more, meaning sector fit is rarely a constraint. Portfolio companies such as Crediwatch in B2B credit intelligence, Alt Mobility in EV fleet leasing, and Driffle in gaming point to a comfort with both deep-tech and marketplace models. Founders can expect a capital partner that brings analytical rigour and a long-term orientation shaped by public markets discipline. The fund is best suited for Indian founders who have early product-market signals and are raising a structured round with multiple investors participating.

investors.name: Stride Ventures
investors.thesis: Provide venture debt to high-growth startups in India
investors.notes: Leading venture debt fund in India; backed OYO, Purplle, Country Delight
investors.writeup: Stride Ventures is one of India's most active and well-regarded venture debt funds, offering non-dilutive debt capital to growth-stage startups looking to extend runway, finance working capital, or fund specific business milestones between equity rounds. Unlike traditional equity investors, Stride provides structured debt instruments that allow founders to retain ownership while accessing meaningful capital, typically in the range of one to fifteen million dollars per transaction. The fund works across sectors including SaaS, FinTech, Consumer, and D2C, and generally looks for startups that already have institutional equity investors on the cap table and demonstrate strong revenue momentum. Stride's portfolio includes well-known Indian consumer and tech brands, reflecting its comfort with businesses at various stages of maturity. For founders, Stride is a practical tool to bridge funding gaps, accelerate growth between Series A and Series B rounds, or complement an ongoing equity raise. Startups approaching Stride should come prepared with clear unit economics, a demonstrated repayment pathway, and ideally an existing institutional lead investor. The team is known for moving efficiently and understanding the operational realities of fast-scaling Indian startups.

investors.name: FreeFlow Ventures
investors.thesis: Build and invest in technology companies with freemium and community-led growth
investors.notes: Venture building studio and early-stage VC
investors.writeup: FreeFlow Ventures sits at the intersection of venture building and early-stage investing, making it a distinctive option for founders who want more than just capital at the pre-seed and seed stages. Their thesis centres on freemium and community-led growth models, meaning they are particularly well-suited for founders building products where organic adoption, product virality, or developer or user communities are central to the go-to-market strategy. They invest across SaaS, consumer tech, B2B, and AI, with cheque sizes ranging from $100k to $500k. As a venture builder, FreeFlow often gets involved early in company formation, which means founders at idea stage or with early prototypes may find them more receptive than a traditional VC. For Indian founders, this hands-on model can be especially valuable for accessing global networks, product positioning support, and distribution playbooks beyond the domestic market. Founders pitching FreeFlow should clearly articulate how their growth loop is freemium or community-driven and demonstrate early signals of organic traction or network effects. Their portfolio orientation toward AI and SaaS makes them a strong fit for B2B software and AI-native product teams targeting global markets from India.

investors.name: Tomorrow Capital
investors.thesis: Invest in founders building tomorrow's most important companies today
investors.notes: India early-stage VC
investors.writeup: Tomorrow Capital is an India-focused early-stage venture capital firm that partners with founders at the Pre-Seed, Seed, and Pre-Series A stages. The firm writes cheques ranging from $100,000 to $1 million, making it a relevant first call for founders raising their initial institutional rounds. Tomorrow Capital concentrates its portfolio across SaaS, Consumer, FinTech, CleanTech, and AI sectors, reflecting a conviction that technology-driven businesses in these verticals will define the next generation of impactful companies. The firm's thesis centers on identifying and backing exceptional founders early, before conventional institutional capital arrives, which means founders can expect a more founder-friendly engagement process and a willingness to evaluate teams and ideas at an earlier stage of validation than larger funds typically require. For Indian startup founders building in these verticals and looking for a stage-appropriate institutional partner who can add value beyond capital, Tomorrow Capital represents a strong fit to explore. Founders should come prepared with a clear articulation of their problem space, early traction or strong founder-market fit, and a view on how their company could become one of the most important businesses in its category.

investors.name: Iron Pillar
investors.thesis: Invest in technology companies built in India for global markets
investors.notes: India technology growth fund; backed Uniphore, Capillary, Darwinbox
investors.writeup: Iron Pillar is a growth-stage technology fund with a sharp focus on enterprise software, SaaS, B2B, AI, and cloud companies headquartered in India but targeting global customers. Their investment mandate is built around a conviction that India can produce world-class technology businesses, not just services firms, and they back founders who are already demonstrating that with real revenue and enterprise traction. The fund typically engages at Series A and Series B, writing cheques between $5M and $30M, making them particularly relevant for founders who have moved past early validation and are ready to accelerate sales, expand internationally, or build out go-to-market infrastructure. The partners bring a mix of operational and investment experience in enterprise technology, which means they engage meaningfully on product positioning, enterprise sales cycles, and global expansion strategy rather than just capital deployment. Portfolio companies like Darwinbox in HR tech and Uniphore in conversational AI reflect their appetite for category-defining enterprise platforms with global applicability. Founders in B2B SaaS or deep-tech enterprise software who are post-product-market fit and eyeing international markets should seriously consider engaging Iron Pillar early in their growth fundraise.

investors.name: GrowthCap Ventures
investors.thesis: Provide growth capital and strategic support to high-potential startups
investors.notes: India growth-focused early-stage VC
investors.writeup: GrowthCap Ventures is an India-focused early-stage venture capital firm that partners with founders building high-potential businesses across SaaS, FinTech, Consumer, and B2B verticals. The firm writes cheques in the range of $250,000 to $3 million, making it relevant for founders raising at the Seed, Pre-Series A, and Series A stages. Beyond capital, GrowthCap Ventures positions itself as a strategic partner, working closely with portfolio companies to navigate the challenges of early growth in the Indian market. Their focus on growth capital suggests an appetite for startups that have demonstrated early traction and are ready to scale operations, expand their team, or deepen their go-to-market efforts. Founders in the SaaS or FinTech space with a clear India-first or India-led global vision are likely to resonate well with their investment approach. Given their stated mandate around strategic support, founders can expect engagement beyond the cheque, including guidance on hiring, partnerships, and subsequent fundraising. Early-stage founders looking for an institutionally minded but founder-friendly partner in India's ecosystem should consider reaching out with a strong narrative around unit economics and growth trajectory.

investors.name: Enzia Ventures
investors.thesis: Invest in technology-driven companies solving fundamental problems
investors.notes: India early-stage VC
investors.writeup: Enzia Ventures is an India-focused early-stage venture capital firm that partners with founders at the Seed and Pre-Series A stages. The firm concentrates on technology-driven startups operating in FinTech, HealthTech, EdTech, SaaS, and B2B markets, backing teams that are using technology to solve real, large-scale problems rather than incremental improvements. Their typical cheque size ranges from $250,000 to $2 million, making them well-suited for founders raising their first institutional round or bridging toward a Series A. Enzia tends to engage closely with portfolio companies at an early stage, which means founders can expect a hands-on relationship rather than a purely financial one. For founders in their target sectors, Enzia is worth approaching with a clear articulation of the problem being solved, the technology differentiation, and early evidence of market traction or customer validation. Given their India-first focus, they are likely attuned to the realities of building in the Indian market, including unit economics constraints, distribution challenges, and regulatory nuances relevant to sectors like FinTech and HealthTech.

investors.name: AdvantEdge Founders
investors.thesis: Help founders get the advantage they need to build their vision
investors.notes: India early-stage VC; backed PlanetSuperheroes, Terribly Tiny Tales
investors.writeup: AdvantEdge Founders is an early-stage venture capital firm focused on the Indian startup ecosystem, writing cheques between $100,000 and $1 million across Pre-Seed, Seed, and Pre-Series A rounds. The firm invests across Consumer, D2C, FinTech, SaaS, and B2B sectors, making it relevant for a wide range of founders building businesses with strong India-market fit. What sets AdvantEdge apart is its founder-first philosophy: the team positions itself as a genuine partner to founders rather than a passive capital provider, offering operational guidance and network access at a stage when those inputs matter most. Their portfolio includes consumer brands like PlanetSuperheroes and content platform Terribly Tiny Tales, signaling an appetite for businesses that combine strong storytelling or community with scalable economics. Founders approaching AdvantEdge should come prepared with a clear articulation of their unfair advantage, a defensible market entry strategy, and an early indication of product-market fit or compelling user traction. The firm is particularly well-suited for founders navigating the often undercapitalized Pre-Seed and early Seed stages in India, where smart money with operational context can be as valuable as the capital itself.

investors.name: Nueva Capital
investors.thesis: Back next-generation founders building category-defining companies
investors.notes: India early-stage micro VC
investors.writeup: Nueva Capital is an India-focused early-stage micro VC that backs founders at the pre-seed and seed stages. Their investment focus spans SaaS, FinTech, Consumer, AI, and B2B businesses, reflecting a broad but deliberate thesis around high-growth technology-driven categories. With cheque sizes ranging from $100k to $500k, they are well-positioned for founders raising initial institutional capital, whether for product development, early team building, or go-to-market experiments. Their stated philosophy centres on partnering with next-generation founders who have the ambition and conviction to build category-defining companies, suggesting they value founder vision and long-term potential as much as early traction metrics. For Indian founders, Nueva Capital represents a practical first call given their stage focus and willingness to engage before product-market fit is fully established. Founders pitching to them should be prepared to articulate a clear market thesis, demonstrate early problem-solution clarity, and show why their category has the potential for outsized outcomes. Their micro VC structure typically implies a more hands-on, founder-friendly engagement style compared to larger institutional funds.

investors.name: Lodha Ventures
investors.thesis: Back technology-enabled businesses transforming Indian markets
investors.notes: Lodha Group family office VC
investors.writeup: Lodha Ventures is the venture investment arm of the Lodha Group, a prominent Indian real estate and infrastructure conglomerate. Operating at the intersection of a family office and an institutional VC, it combines patient capital with deep domain expertise and an established network across India's business and real estate ecosystem. The firm invests at Seed and Series A stages, writing cheques between $500K and $5M, and focuses on Consumer, FinTech, PropTech, SaaS, and B2B startups. Founders benefit from more than just capital: Lodha Group's relationships across financial services, construction, retail, and high-net-worth communities can open doors that traditional VCs often cannot. PropTech and FinTech founders in particular may find meaningful strategic alignment given the group's core business in real estate. Decision-making tends to reflect a founder-friendly, long-term ownership mindset typical of well-run family offices. If your startup is building technology-enabled solutions for large, underpenetrated Indian markets and can leverage a strategic backer with genuine sectoral depth, Lodha Ventures is worth a targeted, well-researched approach.

investors.name: Orios Venture Partners
investors.thesis: Back passionate founders building India's iconic consumer companies
investors.notes: India early-stage VC; backed DriveU, Country Delight, Moxie, Rapido
investors.writeup: Orios Venture Partners is one of India's prominent early-stage venture capital firms, writing cheques between $500K and $5M across Seed, Pre-Series A, and Series A rounds. The firm has a clear affinity for consumer-first businesses and technology-enabled models that tap into India's growing domestic demand, including D2C brands, fintech platforms, SaaS products, and marketplaces. Their portfolio reflects a pattern of backing founders who are building category-defining companies for the Indian market, with names like Country Delight in farm-fresh D2C, Rapido in mobility, and DriveU in driver services demonstrating their appetite for differentiated, high-frequency consumer plays. Founders pitching Orios should come prepared with a compelling India-first narrative, strong unit economics thinking, and evidence of early product-market fit. The team engages actively at the early stage, so expect a hands-on diligence process. Orios is best approached by founders who are solving real Indian consumer pain points at scale, have a differentiated go-to-market strategy, and are building businesses with the potential to become iconic Indian brands over time.

investors.name: 3 Peaks Ventures
investors.thesis: Back resilient founders scaling toward high summits
investors.notes: India early-stage micro VC
investors.writeup: 3 Peaks Ventures is an India-focused micro VC operating at the earliest stages of company building, writing cheques between $100k and $500k at Pre-Seed and Seed. The fund takes its name and philosophy from the idea of founders scaling toward high summits, and the team is drawn to operators who demonstrate resilience, grit, and a clear-eyed view of the hard road ahead. Their sector appetite spans SaaS, FinTech, Consumer, B2B, and AI, giving them broad coverage across the Indian startup landscape without being unfocused. As a micro VC, 3 Peaks tends to move with conviction at early stages where larger funds often hesitate, making them a relevant first institutional conversation for founders who are pre-product-market fit or just beginning to show early traction. Founders approaching 3 Peaks should come prepared to articulate not just the market opportunity but the personal resolve behind why they are the right team to go after it. The fund values the human story behind the business as much as the metrics at this stage. If you are building in India and are at the earliest inflection point of your journey, 3 Peaks Ventures is worth a direct and honest conversation.

investors.name: Upsparks Capital
investors.thesis: Invest in technology startups with global potential from India
investors.notes: India early-stage VC
investors.writeup: Upsparks Capital is an India-based early-stage venture capital firm that backs technology startups at the Pre-Seed, Seed, and Pre-Series A stages. The firm writes cheques ranging from $100,000 to $500,000, making it a relevant partner for founders raising their first or second institutional round. Its investment focus spans SaaS, FinTech, Consumer, AI, and B2B verticals, with a clear preference for startups that are built in India but designed with global scale in mind. Founders who are solving problems with strong product and technology differentiation, and who can articulate a credible path to international markets, are likely to resonate with the Upsparks thesis. The firm operates at the stage where most founders need not just capital but also foundational guidance on go-to-market strategy, early hiring, and investor positioning. For India-based founders building scalable, technology-driven businesses and looking for a hands-on early backer who understands the local ecosystem while keeping an eye on global opportunity, Upsparks Capital is worth engaging early in your fundraising process.

investors.name: Superb Capital
investors.thesis: Back founders building superb companies from the earliest stage
investors.notes: India early-stage micro VC
investors.writeup: Superb Capital is an India-focused early-stage micro VC that partners with founders right from the very beginning, typically at pre-seed and seed stages.
